newsitem.title: USA: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.
newsitem.headline: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.

text.p: Boxed beef this week traded generally lower on light to moderate demand and moderate to heavy offerings, USDA said. Retail and HRI demand was rather light for the abbreviated holiday week.

Immediate retail demand continued light. These present conditions, along with light demand, abundance of boxed beef product and lower live cattle cost forced cutout values lower especially on the Choice cutout, while the Select cut-out values were steady to weak. Choice chuck and round cuts were under pressure all week, with increased downward pressure as the week progressed. Select and Choice middle meats were generally steady, with some weakness developing late in the trading period. Closely trimmed items also traded lower, on rather light demand. Beef trimmings traded lower on light demand and offerings generally moderate to heavy. Fed cattle and blended coarse ground items were generally steady on light to moderate demand and offerings.

Choice chuck primal steady to 2.00 lower; Select and Choice round primal 1.00 to 5.00 lower; Select and Choice loin primal 1.00 to 2.00 lower; Closely trimmed items 1.00 to 2.50 lower; Beef trimmings 4.00 lower; Fed cattle and blended coarse ground items generally steady.

The Estimated Composite of Boxed Beef Cutout values of Choice 1-3 550/700 carcasses Dn 1.79 at 118.02; 700/850 Dn 2.85 at 115.20; Select 1-3 550/700 carcasses Dn .91 at 96.95; 700/850 Dn 1.25 at 95.47.

COW AND BULL CARCASS, BONELESS PROCESSING BEEF, CUTTER COW CUTOUT Despite the holiday interrupted week, slaughter cow numbers remained moderate, which resulted in mostly moderate offerings of lean boneless beef. Demand, however, was moderate to fairly good due to the increased grinding needs for the holiday shopping season, and the lean boneless beef traded slightly higher.

Consequently, a higher cutter carcasses market was seen due to the increase in value of the boneless. In addition, the 100% lean items continue to be under pressure on light demand and moderate offerings. However, tenderloins traded higher on moderate demand and offerings, after many weeks on downward pressure.

Utility carcasses not established; Cutter 2.00 higher; Fresh 90% boneless beef 1.00-2.00 higher; 85% steady to firm; 75% not established; 65% mostly steady. The Cutter cow carcass gross cut-out value for Wednesday, November 27, 1996 was estimated at 66.02 per cwt., up 1.41 from a week ago Friday.
